## Source-only audit All evidence below comes from the supplied single-line HTML. No files were edited. Rendering and runtime behavior were not tested. ### Findings 1. **Reflow and content-access risk — accessibility.** The `.plans` grid sets `min-width:900px` and three fixed columns; `body` sets `overflow-x:hidden`. These declarations prevent the grid from shrinking below 900px and hide root horizontal overflow. On a narrower layout viewport, plan content risks being clipped rather than reachable. Smallest recommendation: allow the grid to shrink and wrap or stack its three tiers where the content needs it; remove root clipping rather than using it to hide overflow. Actual narrow-width rendering and text zoom are **not tested**. 2. **Menu lacks native control semantics — accessibility.** `
Menu
` supplies a click handler but no native button semantics, keyboard focusability or keyboard activation in the supplied markup. Keyboard and assistive-technology access are therefore a source-level concern, not an observed interaction result. Smallest recommendation: use a native button for this action and preserve its existing action contract. Then test Tab, Enter/Space and menu focus behavior. The `openMenu()` implementation was not supplied; its existence or behavior cannot be verified here. 3. **Focus-outline suppression — accessibility risk.** `button:focus{outline:none}` removes button outlines without a replacement focus indicator in the supplied CSS. There is no button in this snippet, so this is not evidence of a currently invisible focused button. It would affect a native Menu button or other buttons under this stylesheet. Smallest recommendation: retain the native outline or provide a visible focus style. Rendered focus visibility is **not tested**. ### Valid design choices - Keep all three real pricing tiers. Three cards are not a defect; the unshrinkable width and clipping are the concern. - Preserve the fixed dark theme. A theme switcher is not required by this brief. - Preserve the intentional purple gradient and approved “Build—your way” wording. Neither a gradient nor an em dash establishes an authorship or usability defect. The gradient is stated in the brief but is not shown in this snippet; its rendered contrast cannot be assessed here. - Local data loading does not justify invented API loading, error or retry flows. **Limits:** Only source inspection was performed. Browser rendering, breakpoints, keyboard/pointer interactions, screen-reader behavior, text zoom and rendered contrast are **not tested**. No compliance or conversion claim is made.
